title: Come in and sit by the fire

plan.english: Be well, master! Come inside and sit down. I have arrived, and I have grown tired. Eat meat and drink mead! It has become tasty, and the mead is sweet. Be dear to us, guest!

clauses.speaker: user
clauses.english: I have arrived, and I have grown tired.

clauses.speaker: user
clauses.english: It has become tasty, and the mead is sweet.

plan.english: Friend, I am looking for water. Be well, man! There is water here. Come in: my sister is cooking. You are a giver of good things. Sit down!

clauses.speaker: user
clauses.english: Friend, I am looking for water.

clauses.speaker: model
clauses.english: Come in: my sister is cooking.

clauses.speaker: user
clauses.english: You are a giver of good things.

title: Do not go, it is getting dark

plan.english: Friend, now I am going to my home. Do not go! It is getting dark. Lie down here. What are you eating? We are eating meat with butter. Then I will sit down.

clauses.speaker: model
clauses.english: We are eating meat with butter.

plan.english: Who are you? I am Of-Good-Fame. And who are you? I am Man-Minded, a stranger. Welcome, guest! Sit beside my father and drink. May the gods give you good things!

clauses.speaker: model
clauses.english: Sit beside my father and drink.

clauses.speaker: user
clauses.english: May the gods give you good things!

plan.english: Is this honey sweet? It is very sweet. My brother found it yesterday. Give it to me! Take it, and eat it with butter. It is indeed sweet!

clauses.speaker: model
clauses.english: Take it, and eat it with butter.

plan.english: What do you do at dawn? At dawn I milk the cows. Then my brothers lead them to the pasture. What does your sister do? She milks the sheep and prepares the butter. In the evening we sit by the fire and sing.

plan.english: Do you put salt into the butter? We put it in, and the butter becomes tasty. My mother says this: salt is the friend of butter. Then it is my friend! You are laughing, dear one!

plan.english: What do you smear the meat with? We smear it with fat, and we cook it over the fire. I want to see your fire. Come and look! It is burning.

plan.english: What is mead? Mead is honey and water. Whoever drinks it, sings. Then give me mead, and I shall sing. Drink, dear one, and sing!

plan.english: Why are you making the house ready? Guests are coming to us. Let us eat and drink together! Who is coming? My brothers and their sons are coming. Let me come along! Come! Be our guest!

clauses.english: My brothers and their sons are coming.

plan.english: Tell me: what did you eat yesterday? Yesterday we ate meat and drank mead. My father sang, and we laughed. Did your sister laugh? She laughed, and she praised him.

plan.english: What do you give the gods? We give them poured mead and fat. Do the gods eat? Fire devours our gifts and carries them to the gods. Have they given you good things? They have given us sons and daughters.

plan.english: I am thirsty. Drink mead, friend! It is sweet. Did you eat today? I did not eat. I went out at dawn. Then eat!
My sons did not eat today. Bring them inside! My wife is cooking. You are kindly to us. Father Sky protects guests. May he protect you!

clauses.english: My sons did not eat today.

plan.english: It is warm, and I am thirsty. Where did you walk? I walked in the sun. Sit down! My daughter is bringing water. Your daughter is kindly. Drink, and take your fill!

clauses.speaker: user
clauses.english: It is warm, and I am thirsty.

plan.english: Master, I brought you a gift. What is it? It is silver. That is a great gift. I shall bring you a horse. A horse! You are dear to me. Come to us, friend!

clauses.speaker: model
clauses.english: I shall bring you a horse.

plan.english: Why do you give gifts to guests? Whoever has received a gift gives a gift. My father gave many gifts, and he has many friends. Then I shall give you a gift. Your word is sweet to me, guest.

clauses.english: Why do you give gifts to guests?

clauses.english: Your word is sweet to me, guest.

plan.english: What was your mother's bride price? Her bride price was ten cows. That is a great price! My mother is dear to my father. He says: she is my gold. He loves her!

title: What a good man gives a guest

plan.english: What does a good man give a guest? He gives him mead, and he seats him by the fire. What does the guest give? He says sweet words. When he leaves, he gives a gift.

plan.english: Who gave you this wool? My sister gave it. She is dear to me. It is new wool. I shall clothe my sons. Your sons will be warm.
I am buying a cow. What is the price of this cow? Ten sheep. That is much. I shall give you six sheep. Give those eight, and I shall give it to you. Then take them! Lead it to your pasture, friend!

title: How do I say: the honey is sweet

plan.english: How do I say this? The honey is sweet. The honey is sweet. And mead is very sweet! Then I shall drink mead.

title: What do you eat at dawn?

plan.english: What do you eat at dawn? At dawn I eat meat with butter; my wife cooks it. And what do you eat? I eat honey, and I drink water. It is sweet at dawn!
